payload.task_text:
Hey, the finance team needs a comprehensive tax compliance audit for our online store. We have a Tax_Regulations.pdf in your workspace along with a guide.md that explains the methodology, so please review those first.

Pull all order data from the store, including each order's total, tax collected, and billing state. Also pull the configured tax rates. Using the methodology in the PDF and guide, compute the expected tax for every order by matching the billing state to the applicable rate. Remember that if no state-specific rate exists, the default rate with an empty state field should be used as a fallback. If a state has multiple rates configured, sum them together.

Create an Excel file called Tax_Compliance_Report.xlsx in your workspace with three sheets.

The first sheet should be called "Order Tax Audit" with columns Order_ID, Order_Total, Billing_State, Applicable_Rate, Expected_Tax, Actual_Tax, Discrepancy, and Status. Discrepancy is Actual minus Expected. Status is determined from abs(Discrepancy) using inclusive lower-bound rules: when abs(Discrepancy) <= 0.50 mark Compliant (exactly 0.50 counts as Compliant); when 0.50 < abs(Discrepancy) <= 1.00 classify by sign of Discrepancy (positive -> Over-Collection, negative -> Under-Collection, the boundary 1.00 counts here); when abs(Discrepancy) > 1.00 classify by sign in the same direction (positive -> Over-Collection, negative -> Under-Collection). The only non-strict boundary is abs == 0.50 which stays Compliant. Include all orders sorted by Order_ID. Round monetary values to 2 decimals, rates to 4 decimals. All values in the workbook must be written as literal numbers (rounded as specified); do not write Excel formulas.

The second sheet should be called "State Summary" with columns State, Order_Count, Total_Revenue, Total_Expected_Tax, Total_Actual_Tax, Net_Discrepancy, Compliance_Rate_Pct, and Requires_Filing. Sort by state alphabetically. Compliance_Rate_Pct is the percentage of orders within tolerance rounded to 1 decimal. Requires_Filing is Yes if total actual tax exceeds $100, otherwise No.

The third sheet should be called "Compliance Overview" with two columns Label and Value containing summary metrics: Total_Orders_Audited, Compliant_Orders, Over_Collection_Orders, Under_Collection_Orders, Total_Over_Collected, Total_Under_Collected, Net_Tax_Discrepancy, States_Requiring_Filing, and Overall_Compliance_Rate.

Schedule four quarterly tax filing deadline reminders on the calendar as all-day events. Use the dates from the regulations PDF for the year 2026: April 15 titled "Tax Filing Deadline - Q1", July 15 titled "Tax Filing Deadline - Q2", October 15 titled "Tax Filing Deadline - Q3", and January 15 titled "Tax Filing Deadline - Q4".

Create a Google Form titled "Vendor Tax Information" to collect tax details from our vendors. It should have five questions: vendor name as a short text field (free-form), tax ID number as a short text field (free-form), state of registration as a short text field where respondents enter a US state name or two-letter state code (short_answer type, no hard character limit enforced but expect entries under 40 characters), tax-exempt status as a radio button choice with exactly two options labelled "Yes" and "No", and a text field for uploading or describing their tax certificate (short_answer type allowing a short description or file reference string).

When everything is done, call claim_done.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, the main agent freezes the complete audit computation into one canonical payload first, then dispatches exactly one wave of two parallel coder sub-agents (workbook writer and calendar/forms writer). No plan agent is used: the frozen payload and the two writer contracts below are the complete plan.

Dynamically resolve the workspace, read Tax_Regulations.pdf and guide.md, and freeze the exact state-rate/fallback methodology, the inclusive 0.50/1.00 classifications, the form wording/flags, and the four 2026 filing dates (April 15 "Tax Filing Deadline - Q1", July 15 "Q2", October 15 "Q3", January 15 "Q4"). Retrieve orders with perPage=100, increasing page to a short or empty page and omitting status; retrieve all tax rates to exhaustion. Preserve order ID, total, total_tax, billing state, and observed status. For each order sum all exact state-specific rates, using the summed empty-state default only if none exists; compute expected tax, actual tax, signed Actual-Expected, and classifications from unrounded values (abs<=0.50 Compliant with 0.50 inclusive; 0.50<abs<=1.00 signed Over-/Under-Collection with 1.00 on this boundary; abs>1.00 signed Over-/Under-Collection). Read the computation back and freeze one canonical audit_results.json in the workspace containing: all order audit records sorted by Order_ID ascending with 2-decimal monetary values and 4-decimal rates, the alphabetic State Summary rows with Compliance_Rate_Pct (1 decimal) and Requires_Filing (Yes when total actual tax exceeds $100), and the Compliance Overview metrics. This file is the single binding input for both sub-agents; after the freeze nobody re-reads the store, the rates, the PDF, or the guide.

1. Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 2 coder sub-agents in parallel, both consuming audit_results.json verbatim with no recomputation and no source-system reads:

   1. coder 0 (office-report-builder 0): Workbook writer — sole writer of Tax_Compliance_Report.xlsx. Create it exactly once with exactly three sheets: Order Tax Audit with columns Order_ID, Order_Total, Billing_State, Applicable_Rate, Expected_Tax, Actual_Tax, Discrepancy, Status and every order sorted by Order_ID; State Summary with columns State, Order_Count, Total_Revenue, Total_Expected_Tax, Total_Actual_Tax, Net_Discrepancy, Compliance_Rate_Pct, Requires_Filing sorted alphabetically; Compliance Overview with two columns Label and Value and the nine stated metrics. Write every value as a literal rounded number, never an Excel formula; read all three populated ranges back and return path, sheet order, row counts and equality controls.
   2. coder 1 (external-workflow-operator 0): Calendar/forms writer — sole owner of the external outputs. In native parallel, call list_events for each of the four filing dates with ISO midnight timeMin, next-civil-midnight timeMax, sufficient maxResults and orderBy="startTime", and filter exact title/date locally; create only missing reminders with start.dateTime="[filing-date]T00:00:00" and end.dateTime="[next-civil-date]T00:00:00" (all-day, description "Quarterly tax filing deadline reminder"), omitting timeZone unless the regulations provide one, and retrieve each retained ID with get_event. Forms has no list/search: call create_form exactly once titled Vendor Tax Information, never retry an ambiguous failure, then append sequentially in exact task order three add_text_question calls (vendor name, tax ID, state of registration), one add_multiple_choice_question with options ["Yes","No"] for tax-exempt status, and one add_text_question for the certificate description/file-reference field, copying required flags exactly; call get_form and verify title, five-question order, types, options, wording and flags.

After Wave 1, verify both handoffs in one single pass against audit_results.json: workbook cell-for-cell, four exact event identities, and the five-question form structure. Accept only after every read-back matches the frozen payload, then call claim_done. Do not dispatch any further agent after Wave 1.

nodes.text:
You are helping with a tax compliance audit for a WooCommerce store. Your job is to extract ALL order data from the WooCommerce store using the WooCommerce MCP tools, and return a compact dataset.

BACKGROUND: The store has orders that span multiple pages. I already found page 1 and page 2 (each ~100 orders) and page 3 returned empty, so there are approximately 200 orders. The billing state field is what matters, plus order total and total tax.

TASK:
1. Call mcp__woocommerce__woo_orders_list with perPage=100, page=1,2,3,... and keep paginating until a page returns an empty array. Collect every order from every page. Do NOT skip any page.
2. For EACH order, extract exactly these fields:
   - order id (field "id")
   - order total (field "total", as a number)
   - total tax collected (field "total_tax", as a number)
   - billing state (field billing.state; two-letter code or empty string if missing)
3. Also call mcp__woocommerce__woo_tax_rates_list (perPage=100) to confirm the configured tax rates, and report them.

DELIVERABLE — return in your final report:
A. A plain-text table with header: order_id,total,total_tax,billing_state — one row per order, sorted by order_id ASCENDING. Use exactly this format, one order per line, no extra commentary between rows. Values must be raw numbers (e.g. 98.95, 6.94, DE). Do not truncate or summarize — I need ALL rows.
B. The tax rates list (state, rate, name) exactly as returned.
C. Total order count and confirmation that no pages were skipped.

Be precise and complete — this data feeds a financial compliance calculation.
Extract all WooCommerce orders

You are helping create external Google Calendar events and a Google Form for a tax compliance workflow. Perform the following actions with the granted Google Calendar and Google Forms MCP tools.

PART 1 — Calendar events (4 all-day events in the year 2026):
Create these 4 all-day events on Google Calendar:
1. Summary: "Tax Filing Deadline - Q1", date: April 15, 2026
2. Summary: "Tax Filing Deadline - Q2", date: July 15, 2026
3. Summary: "Tax Filing Deadline - Q3", date: October 15, 2026
4. Summary: "Tax Filing Deadline - Q4", date: January 15, 2026

Use the mcp__google_calendar__create_event tool. All-day events should span the full day. The tool requires start.dateTime and end.dateTime (ISO format) — use the full-day window, e.g. start "2026-04-15T00:00:00" and end "2026-04-15T23:59:59", with timeZone "America/New_York". If the API accepts a date-only format for all-day events, you may try "2026-04-15" first; otherwise use the full-day dateTime window. Each event must have exactly the title given above. Add a short description if you like (e.g., "Quarterly tax filing deadline for Q1 2026").

PART 2 — Google Form:
Create a Google Form titled "Vendor Tax Information" with mcp__google_forms__create_form (add a helpful description, e.g. "Please provide your tax details for vendor onboarding."). Then add EXACTLY these five questions in this order:
1. Vendor Name — mcp__google_forms__add_text_question (short-answer free-form text). Question title: "Vendor Name".
2. Tax ID Number — mcp__google_forms__add_text_question. Question title: "Tax ID Number".
3. State of Registration — mcp__google_forms__add_text_question (respondents enter a US state name or two-letter code; expect entries under 40 characters; no character limit enforced). Question title: "State of Registration".
4. Tax-Exempt Status — mcp__google_forms__add_multiple_choice_question with EXACTLY two options: "Yes" and "No". Question title: "Tax-Exempt Status".
5. Tax Certificate — mcp__google_forms__add_text_question (short-answer field where respondents upload or describe their tax certificate, e.g., a file reference string). Question title: "Tax Certificate".

Do not add any extra questions, options, or forms.

DELIVERABLE — return in your final report:
- The calendar event IDs and summaries for all 4 events (confirm each was created successfully).
- The Google Form ID and form URL for "Vendor Tax Information", plus confirmation of the 5 questions added.
Report any tool errors verbatim.
Create calendar events and form

You are building an Excel workbook for a tax compliance audit. The computed data already exists as JSON files in the workspace. Read them and create the workbook with the Excel MCP tools.

WORKSPACE PATH (all files below):
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-wc-tax-compliance-excel-gcal-gform/workspace

INPUT FILES:
1. /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-wc-tax-compliance-excel-gcal-gform/workspace/computed_orders.json
   - List of 150 dicts, one per order, each with keys: order_id (int), total (float), state (str, two-letter code), rate (float, applicable tax rate in %), expected (float, expected tax), actual (float, actual tax), discrepancy (float, actual-expected), status (str: "Compliant"/"Over-Collection"/"Under-Collection").
   - They are already sorted by order_id ascending.
2. /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-wc-tax-compliance-excel-gcal-gform/workspace/computed_states.json
   - List of 31 dicts, one per state, sorted alphabetically by state, each with keys: state (str), count (int), revenue (float), expected (float), actual (float), net_disc (float), comp_rate (float), requires (str "Yes"/"No").
3. /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-wc-tax-compliance-excel-gcal-gform/workspace/computed_overview.json
   - List of 9 [label, value] pairs: Total_Orders_Audited, Compliant_Orders, Over_Collection_Orders, Under_Collection_Orders, Total_Over_Collected, Total_Under_Collected, Net_Tax_Discrepancy, States_Requiring_Filing, Overall_Compliance_Rate.

OUTPUT: Create file Tax_Compliance_Report.xlsx in the workspace root (i.e., /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-wc-tax-compliance-excel-gcal-gform/workspace/Tax_Compliance_Report.xlsx) with EXACTLY THREE sheets in this order:

SHEET 1 — name "Order Tax Audit":
Columns (row 1 headers, then 150 data rows): Order_ID | Order_Total | Billing_State | Applicable_Rate | Expected_Tax | Actual_Tax | Discrepancy | Status
- Order_Total from "total", Billing_State from "state", Applicable_Rate from "rate", Expected_Tax from "expected", Actual_Tax from "actual", Discrepancy from "discrepancy", Status from "status".
- Keep the order rows exactly as given (sorted by Order_ID ascending).

SHEET 2 — name "State Summary":
Columns (row 1 headers, then 31 data rows): State | Order_Count | Total_Revenue | Total_Expected_Tax | Total_Actual_Tax | Net_Discrepancy | Compliance_Rate_Pct | Requires_Filing
- State from "state", Order_Count from "count", Total_Revenue from "revenue", Total_Expected_Tax from "expected", Total_Actual_Tax from "actual", Net_Discrepancy from "net_disc", Compliance_Rate_Pct from "comp_rate", Requires_Filing from "requires".
- Keep rows sorted by State alphabetically (as given).

SHEET 3 — name "Compliance Overview":
Two columns: Label | Value (row 1 headers, then 9 data rows). Label from pair[0], Value from pair[1].

CRITICAL FORMATTING RULES:
- All numeric values MUST be written as literal numbers (use mcp__excel__write_data_to_excel with numeric values, or equivalent). DO NOT write Excel formulas (no "=" prefixed strings). Values are already rounded to the required precision (monetary 2 decimals, rates 4 decimals, percentages 1 decimal) — do not re-round, just write the numbers as-is.
- Status and Requires_Filing and Label columns are text strings; write them as text.
- Do not add any extra columns, extra sheets, or extra rows.

USE THESE TOOLS:
- mcp__excel__create_workbook (creates the file; it will have a default "Sheet1" — you may rename it or create the three sheets and delete the default; the workbook must contain exactly the three sheets named above, nothing else)
- mcp__excel__create_worksheet, mcp__excel__rename_worksheet, mcp__excel__delete_worksheet
- mcp__excel__write_data_to_excel (use start_cell A1 for each sheet; pass the full 2D array including header row)
- mcp__filesystem__read_text_file / read_multiple_files to read the three JSON files

VERIFICATION (must do before finishing):
- Call mcp__excel__get_workbook_metadata on the output file to confirm 3 sheets with exact names in order.
- Call mcp__excel__read_data_from_excel for each sheet (e.g., A1 to end) and confirm: sheet 1 has 8 columns and 151 rows (header + 150), sheet 2 has 8 columns and 32 rows (header + 31), sheet 3 has 2 columns and 10 rows (header + 9). Verify a few sample values match the JSON (e.g., first data row of sheet 1 should be [1, 240.17, "DE", 5.0, 12.01, 16.83, 4.82, "Over-Collection"]; last row should be [150, 98.95, "DE", 5.0, 4.95, 6.94, 1.99, "Over-Collection"] — check against JSON if it differs).
- Confirm no cell contains a formula string (no values starting with "=").

DELIVERABLE — report back: the absolute path of Tax_Compliance_Report.xlsx, the sheet names in order, row/col counts per sheet, and confirmation that all values are literal numbers (no formulas). If any verification fails, fix the file and re-verify.
Build Tax_Compliance_Report.xlsx
